title: Morph
description: One black pill on warm white that is the whole player. At rest it is a capsule with the cover, the elapsed time and a waveform tinted from the record. Click it and the clock carries the open: the pill's small elapsed time rises and grows, redrawn as real type at every size with the tracking that size calls for, into tabular figures as tall as the cover, and the title, scrubber and controls hang beneath it on one flush-left column with the time left on its baseline. A few seconds before a song ends the pill reshapes on its own into a wider toast announcing the next one, then folds back. Nothing is a new sheet: width, height and corner radius run on one spring from wherever they are, so you can change your mind mid-morph; the cover and skip button glide to their new places, the waveform bows out, everything else fades through a slight blur as the edge reveals or absorbs it, and the corners stay continuous curves from capsule to squircle.
intent: Translate the one-surface morph of Emil Kowalski's Dynamic Island recreation (https://emilkowal.ski/ui/dynamic-island) and Family's dynamic tray (https://benji.org/family-values) into a now-playing control: states are shapes of one object on interruptible springs, shared elements travel, the rest crossfades with blur so nothing pops.
